finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL after a weak host check. The check is `hostname.endswith("example.com")`, with no leading dot, so it accepts `evilexample.com` or `attacker.com/..` style registrable domains such as `notexample.com`. An attacker can register any domain ending in `example.com` and point it at internal IPs, for example 169.254.169.254, or at a server that redirects there. There is no scheme restriction, no IP pinning or private-range block, and httpx follows no redirects by default, but the attacker-owned host can still resolve to an internal address (DNS rebinding or a plain A record). The response length is returned, which gives a blind/semi-blind oracle. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (".example.com") is defined but unused.
finding.source: `url` query parameter of GET /mirror (unauthenticated, no auth guard)

trace.note: `url: str` taken directly from the request query string
host.endswith("example.com") is a suffix check with no dot boundary, so `evilexample.com` passes. The unused ALLOWED_SUFFIX with its leading dot was evidently intended
c.get(url) requests the original URL string. The host is resolved at request time, so there is no IP validation or pinning

finding.guards_checked: Host suffix check at line 13 is bypassable (no leading dot, so it allows any domain ending in example.com, including attacker-registered ones). No scheme allowlist, no resolved-IP or private/loopback/link-local/metadata block, no DNS pinning. No authentication on the route. The check and the fetch both use the hostname from the same string, so a parser differential is not needed. Redirects are not followed by httpx by default, which limits redirect-based bypasses but not a directly attacker-controlled DNS name.

verdict.guard_found: Only host.endswith("example.com") at mirror.py:13 (suffix check, no dot boundary); ALLOWED_SUFFIX at line 7 is unused. No scheme, IP or auth checks.
verdict.reason: mirror.py:11-16 passes the unauthenticated `url` query param to httpx c.get(url) behind only the bypassable suffix check at line 13, so an attacker-owned host like evilexample.com resolving to an internal IP passes.
